text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — autoscaler unable to provision GPU nodes in Azure westeurope. Queue growth observed for hosted inference (api-prod) and latency SLOs breached for several customers. Pager: maria (oncall). Please ack and triage.

maria (oncall): Acked. I'm seeing a sharp rise in queue length and repeated scale-up attempts failing. Initial impact: ~12% of production requests are queuing >5s, a few 5xxs. Routing policy hasn't triggered fallbacks yet.

ashok: digging in autoscaler logs now. I see Azure returns for VM create: "error: QuotaExceeded" and "OperationNotAllowed" for GPU SKUs. Pasting the relevant autoscaler snippet:

```
[2026-03-10T12:31:10Z] autoscaler: request create vm pool-gpu-eu-1 size=8 sku=Standard_NC6 error=QuotaExceeded: "The subscription has exceeded the regional quota for resource type 'Standard_NC' in location 'westeurope'."
[2026-03-10T12:31:10Z] autoscaler: retrying (attempt 2/5)
[2026-03-10T12:31:20Z] azure-sdk: http 403 || body: {"error": {"code":"OperationNotAllowed","message":"Requested quota for cores exceeds allowed quota"}}
```

kevin: are we seeing any recent capacity events from Azure? Could be a regional outage or their partner blocks.

sarah: I just checked Azure Service Health — no public incident for westeurope. Looks like subscription-level quota enforcement.

alex: can you run `az vm list-usage --location westeurope` and `az vm list-usage --id <subscription>` to confirm current limits and usage? Also check if any quota increases recently canceled.

ashok: running now. Output:

```
$ az vm list-usage --location westeurope --subscription 12345
"virtualMachines": {
  "name": "Standard_NC",
  "currentValue": 64,
  "limit": 64
}
```

ashok: Current GPU SKU usage equals limit (64). Autoscaler requested 8 more GPUs -> hitting the cap.

maria (oncall): That explains it. Do we have spare capacity in other EU regions? We should failover traffic to avoid ongoing customer impact.

kevin: We have a fallback routing policy to preferto-east or eu-north. However, routing policy respects latency SLO and region affinity. For immediate mitigation we can relax affinity for free-tier customers and route new sessions to eu-north.

maria (oncall): I'll flip a temporary override for non-enterprise routes. Command to adjust routing policy (control plane):

```
POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing/overrides
{"scope":"production","selector":"customer_tier:free","action":"route_to:eu-north","expires_in":"00:30:00"}
```

maria (oncall): Doing that now.

opsbot: override applied: non-enterprise production traffic -> eu-north for 30m. (runbook: rollback when queues normalized)

ashok: Meanwhile I'll open an Azure support request to increase regional GPU quota. Creating ticket and attaching autoscaler logs.

ashok: Support ticket created: AZ-INC-99213. ETA from Azure support initially ~4-6 hours for quota increase.

kevin: 4-6h is long. Can we temporarily provision smaller GPU SKUs that still work with our models (e.g., Standard_NC4s) and adjust model concurrency? That would allow partial scaling.

sarah: We have model variants with lower VRAM (quantized). We can flip a runtime config to allow inference on NC4s at reduced batch sizes. That reduces throughput but prevents hard failures.

alex: I'm going to patch the autoscaler to allow fallback skus in this subscription: add priority list [NC6, NC4s, CPU-fallback]. Pushing a quick config change now.

ashok: Patch applied. Autoscaler will accept NC4s for up to 12 nodes. Trying to provision now.

```
[2026-03-10T12:45:03Z] autoscaler: create vm pool-gpu-eu-1 sku=Standard_NC4s size=6 success
[2026-03-10T12:45:12Z] autoscaler: pool-gpu-eu-1 ready
```

maria (oncall): Good — queues are starting to shrink. Latency for impacted customers improving to ~2s p50. Still monitoring.

kevin: Can we also temporarily enable spot instances in eu-north for additional headroom? They are less reliable but help with burst.

ashok: Spinning up 4 spot nodes in eu-north (Standard_NC6_spot). Command:

```
az vm create --resource-group rg-eu-north --name spot-gpu-1 --priority Spot --size Standard_NC6 --subscription 12345
```

ashok: Spot nodes provisioned. Autoscaler attached them as a burst pool.

maria (oncall): Handoff incoming — my shift ends in 25m. Handoff to ashok for continuing ops and follow-up with Azure support. Summarizing:
- Root cause: subscription-level regional GPU quota hit in westeurope (Standard_NC limit reached)
- Immediate mitigations: routing override to eu-north for non-enterprise traffic; allow NC4s; provision spot nodes in eu-north
- Azure ticket AZ-INC-99213 opened for quota increase
- User impact: transient latency increase and slow queues for ~12% of requests, now recovering

ashok: acked. I'll continue monitoring and escalate with Azure if necessary. Maria — please paste any customer-facing template for status update before you go.

maria (oncall): Pasting status update draft for status.redwood.ai:

"We are experiencing elevated latency for inference requests in the EU region due to capacity limits when provisioning GPU instances. We have implemented routing and fallback capacity to reduce customer impact. Our teams are working with Microsoft Azure to increase regional GPU quota. We will post updates as available."

status-bot: Status page update queued — draft posted to incident channel for review: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/az-gpu-capacity-2026-03-10

kevin: quick note — we should also notify Dedicated customers who pinned region/affinity that they might see rerouting if capacity remains constrained. Ops to compile list.

ashok: Azure just responded to the ticket: initial review shows request valid; we have option to raise soft limit now but need engineering confirmation for near-term autoscaling behavior. Reply: "We can increase Standard_NC quota by 32 if you provide expected usage pattern." I replied with our autoscaler demand graphs and asked for expedited increase.

sarah: For postmortem: add step to proactively request higher regional limits when utilization >70% for 24h and add automated quota-check to pre-warn oncall 48h earlier.

alex: Also adding a playbook entry: if quota error received, apply fallback SKUs + routing override + spot provisioning in that order.

maria (oncall): I'm logging off now — handoff complete. ashok is primary. Thanks all.

ashok: Taking over. Monitoring: queue length at 940 -> 420 after fallbacks. p95 latency down from 8.2s -> 2.9s. Continuing watch and liaising with Azure.

(2h later)
ashok: Azure increased Standard_NC quota in westeurope by +32 (approved). Autoscaler resumed normal NC6 provisioning.

```
[2026-03-10T14:58:10Z] autoscaler: create vm pool-gpu-eu-1 sku=Standard_NC6 size=8 success
[2026-03-10T14:59:00Z] autoscaler: new capacity attached, queue drained
```

maria (oncall): Marking incident RESOLVED — services recovered, p95 latency back to normal. Final impact: ~45 minutes of degraded latency for a subset of traffic, mitigations applied minimized errors. Follow-ups:
- RFC for proactive quota requests and automated pre-warn alerts
- Runbook updates to include fallback SKU list and routing override commands
- Ops: review Dedicated customer reroute notification process

status-bot: Incident resolved on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/az-gpu-capacity-2026-03-10 (root cause: subscription regional GPU quota exhausted) :white_check_mark:

ashok: Adding timeline and logs to the postmortem doc. We'll include Azure ticket AZ-INC-99213 and action items. Closing thread.
